newsitem.title: USA: US baby-boomers saving more for retirement - study.
newsitem.headline: US baby-boomers saving more for retirement - study.

text.p: Baby boomers are saving more than ever before for retirement but they are still way off from saving enough to maintain their current standard of living once they leave the workforce, according to a study released Wednesday.

Baby boomers are saving 38.5 percent of the money they will need in order to maintain the same standard of living in retirement that they enjoy while working, the Merrill Lynch study showed. Boomers, identified as people born between 1946 and 1964, saved 35.9 percent of the necessary funds in 1996.
Merrill Lynch attributed the increase to a surge in savings from those who have hit their fifties.
"Although it is a late start, it seems people are heeding the message to increase their retirement savings," Merrill Lynch Vice Chairman John Steffens said in a statement.

The survey of 2,000 households also found that Baby Boomers are not prepared for short-term problems, like job losses or unexpected expenses. The survey found that only half of all Baby Boomers have more than three months of income saved up in the form of liquid assets, what Merrill Lynch considers as the required amount to be prepared for short-term emergencies.
